# Proverbs 5 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** My-son, to-my-wisdom attend, to-my-understanding incline your-ear,

**2** To-keep discretion, and-knowledge your-lips will-guard.

**3** For honey drip [the]-lips-of [the]-strange-woman, and-smoother than-oil her-palate.

**4** But-her-end [is]-bitter like-wormwood, sharp like-a-sword-of mouths.

**5** Her-feet go-down to-death; her-steps take-hold-of Sheol.

**6** Lest [the]-path-of life she-ponder, her-tracks wander — she-does-not-know.

**7** And-now, sons, hear to-me, and-do-not-depart from-[the]-words-of my-mouth.

**8** Keep-far from-upon-her your-way, and-do-not-draw-near to-[the]-door-of her-house,

**9** Lest you-give to-others your-splendor, and-your-years to-[the]-cruel-one,

**10** Lest strangers be-filled [with]-your-strength, and-your-toils [be] in-[the]-house-of a-foreigner,

**11** And-you-groan at-your-end, when-is-consumed your-flesh and-your-body,

**12** And-you-say, 'How I-hated discipline, and-correction my-heart despised,

**13** And-I-did-not-listen to-[the]-voice-of my-teachers, and-to-my-instructors I-did-not-incline my-ear.

**14** In-almost every evil I-was, in-[the]-midst-of [the]-assembly and-congregation.'

**15** Drink waters from-your-[own]-cistern, and-flowing-[waters] from-[the]-midst-of your-[own]-well.

**16** Should-your-springs be-scattered outside, in-[the]-plazas streams-of water?

**17** Let-them-be for-you alone, and-not for-strangers with-you.

**18** Let-your-fountain be blessed, and-rejoice with-[the]-wife-of your-youth.

**19** A-doe-of loves, a-gazelle-of grace — let-her-breasts satisfy-you at-all-times; in-her-love be-intoxicated always.

**20** And-why will-you-be-intoxicated, my-son, with-a-strange-woman, and-embrace [the]-bosom-of a-foreign-woman?

**21** For before [the]-eyes-of YHWH [are the]-ways-of a-man, and-all his-tracks He-ponders.

**22** His-[own]-iniquities will-capture-him — the-wicked — and-in-[the]-cords-of his-sin he-will-be-held.

**23** He will-die for-lack-of discipline, and-in-[the]-greatness-of his-folly he-will-go-astray.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **5:3-4**: Nofet — 'honey from the comb,' the purest, most desirable honey. The contrast between sweetness and wormwood (la'anah) is deliberate.

- **5:15-18**: Extended water metaphor for marital fidelity. Cistern/well/fountain = one's own wife; springs scattered abroad = infidelity.

- **5:19**: Explicit erotic language — 'let her breasts satisfy you' (yeravvukha) — using the root r-v-h, 'to be saturated/intoxicated.'

— EMET
